clue.text: Setting to delight certain animal-welfare groups

definitions.text: Setting to delight certain animal-welfare groups

parts.words: Setting to delight certain animal-welfare groups
parts.note: a sundown that pleases shepherds, cheekily called animal-welfare groups, recalls the weather proverb about a crimson evening glow

explanation.surface: A scheme designed to please charities that protect animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' reads as an arrangement but means the sun going down; the old rhyme says a glowing sunset is the shepherd's delight, and shepherds look after their flocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The weather proverb promises fine weather to shepherds when the sunset glows, so this sundown delights flock-keepers.

clue.text: Cool tune I composed for vocal presentation

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cool melody was written to be performed by singers.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill of clear, expressive public speaking is delivery by voice.

clue.text: Duck in this way put to some purpose

parts.note: so means in this way, as in 'do it so'
to use something is to put it to some purpose

explanation.surface: A duck behaves in this manner to serve some end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird but is the verb: to plunge someone into water.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to drench them by plunging them under water, the soaking sense of the verb.

clue.text: Giving up, having lied badly during first year of power

indicators.note: during says the jumbled word sits inside the other pieces, lasting through them
first picks out the opening letter of the word year

parts.note: read as 'in G': 'of' standing for 'in', and G, the symbol for gravitational force (as in G-force), standing for power

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters of lied are mangled

explanation.surface: A leader resigns after lying clumsily in their first year in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns LIED into IELD, which goes 'during' Y plus IN G. 'of power' as IN G is a real stretch: G-force stands in for power, and even the puzzle's blogger doubted it.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrendering or conceding something is ceding it, the submissive sense of the verb.

clue.text: Poles carry documents

parts.note: to tote something is to carry it
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a document; MS also serves as its plural

explanation.surface: Poles are bringing their papers with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means tall carved posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved tribal posts of the Pacific Northwest, bearing clan emblems, are a kind of pole.

clue.text: Upsetting to sailors they may maroon

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning or disturbing, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being cast away upsets seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that cut people off from others keep them alone, as being stranded on an island does.

clue.text: Island holiday, start it in first-class accommodation

indicators.note: the start of the word holiday is its opening letter
in, with accommodation, says one piece is housed within another
accommodation means housing, so the first-class piece houses the word it

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A holiday on an island, beginning in a luxury suite.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, written AI. 'holiday, start' is loose: it means the start of 'holiday'. Haiti is strictly a country on the island of Hispaniola.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean nation shares the land mass of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Surprised as I am to say this, not once did I excel

definitions.text: Surprised as I am to say this

explanation.surface: Someone admits with surprise that they never shone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the phrase's words in another order: 'I never did well', a confession of never excelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment; and, with its words taken in another order, an admission of lifelong mediocrity.

clue.text: Restoration? Check the financial summary

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, and a rein is a check
a statement of account summarises finances

explanation.surface: Return to power? Look at the accounts first.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone back in a former post is restoring them to it.

clue.text: Hidden mole at university meant to hear profit results

indicators.note: hidden is used loosely here to mean disguised, so the letters of mole are rearranged
to hear says the word meant is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the word meant is said aloud, giving its sound without the A

explanation.surface: A spy hidden at a university was supposed to hear the profit figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it disguises MOLE as EMOL; there is no hidden run. 'to hear' turns MEANT into MENT by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary, fee or other payment for work is a gain or earnings for the person paid.

clue.text: Unfortunately, I love a sailor's sweetheart

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, I love someone who belongs to a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor is Popeye, the spinach-eating cartoon hero, whose girlfriend is Ms Oyl.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Popeye cartoons, the spinach-eating seaman's girlfriend is the skinny Ms Oyl.

clue.text: Insect left flower

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A bug left a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' wants to be a bloom but means a thing that flows: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: This small wingless parasite of hair and feathers is a kind of bug.

clue.text: Barrier erected by people making angry exclamation?

parts.note: a dam is a barrier built across water
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A dam built by a country gets its people swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting this word in fury is cursing, the expletive use of eternal punishment.

clue.text: Is an ant's evolution heralding a beastly sign of division?

definitions.text: heralding a beastly sign of division?

indicators.note: evolution means gradual change, so these letters develop into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plain word with its S

explanation.surface: Does the way an ant changes announce a creature splitting in two?
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry ('heralding') a beast shown rising out of the middle of a band dividing the shield is said to be born from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry uses this term, French for 'being born', for a creature shown emerging from the middle of a dividing band.

clue.text: Trade-in car, cash sweetener provided

indicators.note: to trade is to exchange, so the letters of these words are swapped around

explanation.surface: A trade-in car and some cash are added as a sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade-in' reads as one word, but 'Trade' is the signal and 'in' joins 'car' and 'cash' as the letters to rework.
explanation.definitionFit: This artificial sugar substitute is a sweetener; 'sweetener' also slyly means an inducement in the surface.

clue.text: Finding a doctor in Ulster possibly could be a struggle

indicators.note: in says the doctor is placed inside the overcoat

parts.note: an Ulster is a long heavy overcoat, so it is one example of a coat
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Finding a physician in Northern Ireland might be a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like Northern Ireland but is a long overcoat; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or battle is a hard struggle against an opponent.

clue.text: Officer on board putting craft before lover

parts.note: a boat is a craft
swain is an old poetic word for a young lover

explanation.surface: An officer on the ship puts his vessel ahead of his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's petty officer in charge of rigging and deck crew holds this post.

clue.text: Rising on-line-delivery service

parts.note: something that climbs a slope while running on a wire rope, carrying passengers, read as a service delivered along a line

explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' suggests internet shopping, but it means running along a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger cabin hauled up a mountainside by a wire rope is a form of transport.

clue.text: Italian source of exotic vine on English church

indicators.note: exotic means foreign or strange, so the letters of vine are made unfamiliar

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Italian origin for a foreign grape plant growing on an English church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' turns VINE into VENI.
explanation.definitionFit: This lagoon city in north-east Italy is a place from which goods such as glass come.

clue.text: Engine part, half of machine's fast revolution

indicators.note: revolution means turning over, so the letters are churned into a new order
half of the possessive word machine's is its first four letters

explanation.surface: Half of a machine's rapid spinning comes down to one engine component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes MACH from 'machine's'; 'revolution' reworks MACH plus FAST.
explanation.definitionFit: This rotating rod with lobes opens and closes the valves in an engine.

clue.text: Tie off fruit tree, put out to grass again

indicators.note: off says the letters of the word tie are taken away from the fodder
put out means disturbed, so what remains of the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Untie a fruit tree and put it out to pasture again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie off' removes T, I and E from FRUIT TREE; 'put out' scrambles the remaining F, R, U, T, R, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay sod on bare ground is to cover it with lawn once more.

clue.text: Like Spooner's duff reel, not a good transaction

indicators.note: Spooner's names the Oxford don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

explanation.surface: Unfair treatment, like a badly danced Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' is British slang for bad; a reel is a lively Scottish dance. Swapping the opening sounds of DUFF and REEL gives 'ruff deel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment that leaves someone worse off is a poor bargain.

clue.text: After a loss, relative is to get rid of bonds

indicators.note: loss says a letter is lost from the relative

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: After a death, a relative has to shake off family ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a loss' takes the A off AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from cords or knots is to loosen what binds them.

clue.text: English town, of course

parts.note: a town in Surrey, the county south of London, famed for its racecourse where the Derby is run; 'of course' is both 'naturally' and 'of the racecourse'

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but points to the town's famous racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: This Surrey town, south of London, hosts the Derby horse race on its downs.

clue.text: Where some creatures live is heart-breaking

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: Where some animals live is a heartbreaking place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-breaking' reads as one word, but 'breaking' is the signal acting on 'heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's or badger's underground den goes by this name in British country usage.

clue.text: Make a grave commitment

parts.note: a solemn pledge reads instead as committing a body to a grave

explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like 'serious' but is a burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury the dead is to commit them to the ground.

clue.text: New car in tune? Are you sure?

definitions.note: the question voices doubt, standing for the state of not knowing for certain

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Is a brand-new car really in tune? Do you know that for certain?
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone whether they are sure expresses doubt, being unsure.

clue.text: Old transport system sounding cheaper than it probably was

definitions.text: Old transport system sounding cheaper than it probably was

parts.words: Old transport system sounding cheaper than it probably was
parts.note: a Victorian bicycle with one huge and one tiny wheel, named after two small old coins, so its name suggests a trifling price

explanation.walkthrough: The name joins two tiny pre-decimal British coins, worth together barely more than a penny, so it sounds very cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: The high Victorian bicycle with one huge and one tiny wheel is named after two small pre-decimal coins.
